author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Plutarch, Life of Crassus (Plut. Crass.), c. 100-110 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Primary narrative source for Crassus's life. Written ~150 years after his death. Plutarch draws on lost earlier sources including Livy and Sallust. Some passages are moralizing — Plutarch uses Crassus's greed as a cautionary theme.

author: Cassius Dio
citation_detail: Cassius Dio, Roman History Books 37-40, c. 210-230 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Most complete continuous narrative covering the First Triumvirate and Parthian campaign. Written ~260 years after events. Draws heavily on Livy and Augustan-era sources.

author: Appian of Alexandria
citation_detail: Appian, Civil Wars (Bella Civilia) Books 1-2, c. 150-160 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Detailed narrative of Spartacus revolt and early triumviral period. Book 1 covers Spartacus; Book 2 covers the First Triumvirate. Draws on lost sources including Livy and Asinius Pollio.

author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
citation_detail: Cicero, Letters (Epistulae ad Atticum, ad Familiares), 68-43 BCE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Contemporary correspondence mentioning Crassus during the triumviral period and Parthian campaign. Cicero navigated between Crassus, Pompey, and Caesar. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5: Cicero's letters reflect his personal and political biases; specific section references need verification.

author: Sallust
citation_detail: Sallust, Histories, c. 35 BCE. Patrick McGushin (trans.), Oxford (1992).
notes: Near-contemporary history covering the 70s-60s BCE, including Spartacus revolt and Crassus-Pompey rivalry. Survives only in fragments. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5: fragmentary preservation, referenced through later quotations.

author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Plutarch, Life of Pompey (Plut. Pomp.), c. 100-110 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Parallel biography covering Crassus-Pompey rivalry and the First Triumvirate from Pompey's perspective. Overlap with Plutarch's Life of Crassus.

author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Plutarch, Life of Caesar (Plut. Caes.), c. 100-110 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Covers Crassus's role in the First Triumvirate from Caesar's perspective.

author: Bruce A. Marshall
citation_detail: Marshall, Bruce A. (1976). Crassus: A Political Biography. Adolf M. Hakkert.
notes: Modern scholarly biography focused on Crassus's political career. Analyzes his wealth, power base, and role in the First Triumvirate.

author: Allen Mason Ward
title_en: Marcus Crassus and the Late Roman Republic
citation_detail: Ward, Allen Mason (1977). Marcus Crassus and the Late Roman Republic. University of Missouri Press.
notes: Comprehensive modern study of Crassus's political influence, wealth, and role in the collapse of the Republic.

author: Gareth C. Sampson
title_en: The Defeat of Rome: Crassus, Carrhae and the Invasion of the East
citation_detail: Sampson, Gareth C. (2008). The Defeat of Rome: Crassus, Carrhae and the Invasion of the East. Pen & Sword Military.
notes: Modern study of the Parthian campaign and Carrhae. Analyzes military decisions, intelligence failures, and aftermath.

author: Erich S. Gruen
title_en: The Last Generation of the Roman Republic
citation_detail: Gruen, Erich S. (1974). The Last Generation of the Roman Republic. University of California Press.
notes: Major modern study of the late Republic. Analyzes Crassus's political position and the dynamics of the First Triumvirate as informal political arrangement.
